description: What the Mac and the desktop client both say and decide for a presentation, a Markdown document the engine splits into slides (writing.structure gives each slide's lines, heading, notes and images). slideTitles and slideNotes are the words of a slide in the rail; slideAtLine is which slide a line of the source belongs to (a slide's last line counts, as the endLine the engine sends is the line after it); hint is the line under the source. showCommands maps a key or a click to what a slide show does, showStates walks its position (a step is an apply of a command or a reconcile to a new slide count, and says whether the show must close and where it stands), showStage fits the 16:9 stage into a viewport and slideMetrics sizes a presented slide's title, spacing and padding from the stage. layout lays the pane out from the size of its body (under the header, footer included): thumbnails beside the stage when the width reaches the rail plus the smallest stage and the margins, else a strip of numbers over it; the stage is the largest 16:9 rectangle that fits the room left, between the smallest and the largest stage, centered in it; rects are x, y, width and height from the body's top left. layout.metrics are the Mac's constants (PaneLayoutContentMetrics) the desktop client holds as tokens. Both clients pass every case.

hint.line: Title → appears on slide · regular text → your notes · --- → new slide

slideAtLine.name: the first line of a slide
the line a slide ends before still belongs to it
a line between two slides belongs to none
the first line of the next slide
the first slide wins when two meet

showStates.name: a position past the last slide starts on it
the position stays between the first and the last slide
fewer slides move the position and none close the show

cases.name: the smallest body has numbers and the smallest stage
a body smaller than the smallest is laid out as the smallest
one point short of the thumbnails the numbers stay
the thumbnails come at the boundary
a wide body gives the largest stage
